meta.title: Curated CWE knowledge subset for Assignment 2
meta.disclaimer: This is a curated teaching subset derived from well-known public CWE/MITRE catalog facts (names, high-level descriptions, common mitigations, and published relationships). It is not an official MITRE dump, not a complete CWE database, and not a substitute for cwe.mitre.org.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
entries.description: The software constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally influenced input without neutralizing special elements that can modify the intended command.

mitigations.title: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements
mitigations.text: Bind user values as parameters instead of concatenating them into the SQL string.

mitigations.title: Least-privilege database accounts
mitigations.text: The application account should only have the statements it needs (no DROP/admin).

mitigations.title: Allowlist dynamic identifiers
mitigations.text: If table or column names must be dynamic, allowlist them rather than interpolating raw input.

entries.detection_notes: String-concatenated SQL passed to Statement.executeQuery / executeUpdate is a common teaching pattern.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
entries.description: The software does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output used as a web page.

mitigations.title: Context-appropriate output encoding
mitigations.text: HTML-encode (or JSON/attribute/URL-encode, depending on sink) untrusted data before writing it into a page.

mitigations.title: Use auto-escaping templates
mitigations.text: Prefer frameworks that escape by default; avoid writing raw markup from request parameters.

entries.detection_notes: HTML markup concatenated with a request/comment string without an encode helper is a common teaching pattern.

entries.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
entries.description: The software uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to stay under a restricted parent directory, but does not properly neutralize special elements such as '..' sequences.

mitigations.title: Resolve and constrain the path
mitigations.text: Normalize/canonicalize the path and reject it if it does not remain under the intended base directory.

mitigations.title: Allowlist file identifiers
mitigations.text: Map user input to known file IDs rather than concatenating raw path segments.

entries.detection_notes: java.io.File constructed by concatenating a caller-supplied relative path is a common teaching pattern.

entries.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
entries.description: The application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, which can lead to unexpected object graphs or control flow.

mitigations.title: Do not deserialize untrusted Java objects
mitigations.text: Prefer data-only formats (JSON, protobuf) with explicit schemas over ObjectInputStream on untrusted input.

mitigations.title: Constrain types if deserialization is required
mitigations.text: Use look-ahead / type allowlists rather than unrestricted readObject on attacker-controlled streams.

entries.detection_notes: ObjectInputStream.readObject on an InputStream is a common teaching pattern. This catalog does not include gadget chains or exploit payloads.

entries.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
entries.description: The software contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key, which it uses for its own inbound authentication, outbound communication to external components, or encryption of internal data.

mitigations.title: Load secrets from the environment or a secret store
mitigations.text: Do not ship passwords or API keys as string literals; inject them at deployment time.

mitigations.title: Rotate default credentials
mitigations.text: Default or sample passwords in source must never be used in a real system.

entries.detection_notes: Assignments of password/apiKey/secret to a string literal are the teaching pattern. Examples in this repo use fake values such as admin/password.

entries.name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
entries.description: The software stores or transmits sensitive data using a cryptographic algorithm that is known to be weak, obsolete, or otherwise inappropriate for the protection needed.

mitigations.title: Use currently recommended algorithms
mitigations.text: Prefer SHA-256/SHA-3 family hashes and modern authenticated encryption; do not use MD5, DES, or RC4 for security.

mitigations.title: Use vetted crypto libraries
mitigations.text: Call maintained platform APIs rather than implementing or selecting obsolete ciphers by name.

entries.detection_notes: MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5") versus SHA-256 is the teaching contrast in the seed.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic
entries.description: The software constructs a data query using externally influenced input without neutralizing special elements that can modify the intended query logic.

mitigations.title: Separate query structure from values
mitigations.text: Use bind variables / parameterized APIs for SQL, LDAP, and similar query languages.

entries.detection_notes: Parent class of SQL injection (CWE-89) in the CWE hierarchy used here.

entries.name: SQL Injection: Hibernate
entries.description: An ORM / Hibernate-style query is constructed with untrusted input in a way that can change the intended query.

mitigations.title: Use parameterized ORM queries
mitigations.text: Bind values through the ORM API rather than concatenating HQL/SQL.

entries.detection_notes: Related child of CWE-89; included so relationship walks have a target. Not represented as its own Java seed unit.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Output Used by a Downstream Component ('Injection')
entries.description: The software constructs all or part of a command, query, or other structured message using externally influenced input without neutralizing special elements.

mitigations.title: Neutralize for the downstream interpreter
mitigations.text: Encode or parameterize for the specific sink (SQL, HTML, OS, LDAP) rather than applying a generic sanitize.

entries.detection_notes: Injection class covering XSS and query neutralization parents used in this subset.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
entries.description: The software receives input from an upstream component but does not neutralize special characters that could be interpreted as web-scripting elements.

mitigations.title: HTML-encode untrusted page content
mitigations.text: Strip or encode script-related tags before reflecting input into HTML.

entries.detection_notes: More specific XSS variant under CWE-79.

entries.name: Improper Input Validation
entries.description: The product receives input or data but does not validate or incorrectly validates that the input has the properties required to process it safely.

mitigations.title: Validate against a spec
mitigations.text: Check type, length, range, and encoding of inputs close to the trust boundary. Validation complements (does not replace) parameterized queries and output encoding.

entries.detection_notes: Broad ancestor used for relationship walks; not a seed-unit label by itself.

entries.name: Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference
entries.description: The software uses a name or reference to access a resource, but the name/reference resolves to a resource that is outside the intended control sphere.

mitigations.title: Resolve names before use
mitigations.text: Canonicalize identifiers and compare them against the intended namespace.

entries.detection_notes: Parent of path traversal (CWE-22) in this subset.

entries.name: Relative Path Traversal
entries.description: The software uses external input to construct a pathname that includes relative path sequences such as '..' sequences.

mitigations.title: Reject parent-directory segments after normalize
mitigations.text: After resolving the path, ensure it still starts with the allowed root.

entries.detection_notes: Child of CWE-22; teaching samples in the seed use generic path concatenation rather than a dedicated relative-path unit.

entries.name: Absolute Path Traversal
entries.description: The software uses external input to construct a pathname that can resolve to an absolute location outside the intended directory.

mitigations.title: Reject absolute paths from callers
mitigations.text: Treat user-supplied absolute paths as out of bounds unless explicitly allowed.

entries.detection_notes: Child of CWE-22.

entries.name: Improper Control of Dynamically-Managed Code Resources
entries.description: The software does not properly restrict the resources that can be loaded or executed dynamically, such as deserialized objects or reflective code.

mitigations.title: Restrict dynamic loading
mitigations.text: Allowlist types and avoid executing attacker-influenced serialized graphs.

entries.detection_notes: Parent of CWE-502 in this subset.

entries.name: Improper Authentication
entries.description: The software does not sufficiently verify that an actor claiming an identity is who they claim to be.

mitigations.title: Use a real authentication mechanism
mitigations.text: Do not bake identities or shared secrets into source; verify credentials through a dedicated store.

entries.detection_notes: Parent used for CWE-798 relationship walks in this curated subset.

entries.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
entries.description: The software contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for inbound authentication, outbound communication, or similar purposes.

mitigations.title: Remove password literals
mitigations.text: Read passwords from a secret manager or environment; never commit real passwords.

entries.detection_notes: Child of CWE-798. Seed units use fake teaching passwords only.

entries.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
entries.description: The software uses a hard-coded cryptographic key for authentication, encryption, or integrity protection.

mitigations.title: Use a key-management path
mitigations.text: Load keys from a KMS or protected store rather than embedding them in source.

entries.detection_notes: Child of CWE-798.

entries.name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
entries.description: The software stores or transmits sensitive data using an encryption scheme that is theoretically sound but is not strong enough for the required protection.

mitigations.title: Choose adequate key sizes and algorithms
mitigations.text: Follow current platform guidance; avoid known-broken ciphers and short keys.

entries.detection_notes: Parent of CWE-327 in this subset.

entries.name: Use of Weak Hash
entries.description: The software uses a hashing algorithm that does not provide enough protection for the required use (for example MD5 or SHA-1 when a stronger digest is needed).

mitigations.title: Use a strong digest
mitigations.text: Use SHA-256 or better for integrity; do not use MD5 as a security hash.

entries.detection_notes: Child of CWE-327; the seed MD5 unit is labeled CWE-327 as the broader class.
